text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended a light pre-holiday trading session firmer. Front month August last traded $3.00 higher at $313.70 per tonne, while October added $1.20 to close at $302.50 per tonne.

In New York raw sugar futures settled firmer after a late round of producer short-covering fueled prices to the day's highs. Most-active July closed 10 points firmer at 10.80 cents/lb while October added 7 points to close at 10.67 cents/lb. The outer months gained 3 to 6 points. July could come under speculative pressure as speculators retain a huge net long position with open interest at 82,412 lots as of early Thursday. News that the Cuban 1996/97 crop may be lower than had been expected failed to impress the market.

CUBA - Only recently Gilberto Llerena, the vice minister of Cuba's sugar industry, said that drought, Hurricane Lili and the effects of the Helms Burton law would limit production and that the total would be only slightly in excess of last season's figure. However, the Cuban president Fidel Castro is even more pessimistic and recently said that this year's harvest will not reach the 4.45 mn tonnes, tel quel, achieved in 1995/96.

THAILAND - Sugar exports in February 1997 amounted to 488,722 tonnes, down from last year's 574,856 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first four months of 1996/97 (November/February) up to 992,867 tonnes compared to 1.030 mn tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 4.653 mn tonnes against 3.847 mn tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in November/February 1996/97 were Indonesia with 376,500 tonnes whites against 153,977 tonnes, South Korea with 160,200 tonnes raws against 178,624 tonnes, Japan with 115,874 tonnes, down from 187,106 tonnes and Malaysia with 59,000 tonnes, up from 39,206 tonnes.

NEW ZEALAND - Sugar imports in March 1997 reached 19,367 tonnes, raw value, down from 37,589 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the January/March 1997 up to 48,928 tonnes against 70,367 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1996 reached 263,774 tonnes compared to 210,379 tonnes in 1995. The major country of origin in the first quarter of 1997 was Australia with 38,843 tonnes raws, down from 55,979 tonnes and 9,169 tonnes whites against 13,182 tonnes. Sugar exports in January/March 1997 reached 3,881 tonnes, hardly changed from last year's 3,815 tonnes. Total exports in 1996 amounted to 21,407 tonnes against 20,270 tonnes in 1995. The major country of destination in January/March 1997 was French Polynesia with 1,163 tonnes whites against 481 tonnes.

GERMANY - Sugar consumption in March 1997 amounted to 227,615 tonnes, raw value, down from 244,549 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative consumption in the first half of 1996/97 (October/March) up to 1.449 mn tonnes, slightly below last year's 1.463 mn tonnes. Total consumption in 1995/96 reached 3.076 mn tonnes against 2.995 mn tonnes in 1994/95. Sugar output in the first half of 1996 amounted to 4.546 mn tonnes against 4.140 mn tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total output in 1995/96 was 4.158 mn tonnes against 3.991 mn tonnes in 1994/95.
